comments.body: A second path rings it too: when the adopting session's turn ends, went_idle treats that as @human going idle and sends a 'still unread' wake for each group. So the agent got two wakes per group: the stall check's wake_again, then 'still unread' once its turn ended.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: The stall check also posts to the group as @muster telling the agents '@human has not read #7 ... 5 minutes after it was posted', as though the human were a stuck agent holding the group up.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A Claude Code session in a pane that runs any msg verb with `--as @human` gives the human participant that session's pane and inbox. From then on the daemon treats the human as an agent in that pane: `muster msg who` lists `@human` as "human (working)" with its unread "rung, and is at work", and the stall check (`stalls.rs`, `Act::WakeAgain`) types the human's wake into the agent's prompt.

Seen on 0.18.2-dev, 2026-10-25. From pane umber (p2eg0vf7he) I ran `msg group new otter-name --as @human`, `group add ... --as @human` and `post --as @human` to set up a demo. Two minutes after agents posted to the group, the daemon logged `msg.group.stalled` for member `@human` with `pane: p2eg0vf7he`, then `msg.group.woken_again ... via p2eg0vf7he` and `msg.rang name=@human pane=p2eg0vf7he`. Umber's Claude Code received `[muster] otter-name: 4 new (#7-10), 1 to you ...` as a prompt. `state.json` then held `{"name":"@human","inbox":{"socket":"/tmp/cc-socks/77338.sock"},"pane":"p2eg0vf7he"}`.

The cause looks to be `identify_reporting` in `muster-msg/src/service.rs`: for `as_name`, `may_become` exempts `HUMAN` from the name-in-use check, and `adopt(name, caller)` then copies the caller's addresses onto `@human`. Acting as the human from a session should move no addresses, the way a script with none acts as anyone. Likely also at risk: a later verb from that session without `--as` being looked up as `@human` by its addresses, so a plain `muster msg read` there would read the human's unread.

Workaround until fixed: act as the human from a shell with no addresses, `env -u MUSTER_PANE -u CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET muster msg ... --as @human`.
title: An agent that acts --as @human takes over the human's pane and inbox, so the human's wakes are typed into that agent
